deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 23-25). π̂ is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}: a free profinite group on generators l_0, l_1, l_∞ subject to l_∞ l_1 l_0 = 1. L_i is the closed subgroup generated by l_i, so L_i ≅ Ẑ. Σ̂^! (written Γ̂^!/Ê^! on the previous page; the notation shifts) is the group of 'admissible' automorphisms, i.e. those taking each l_i to a conjugate of a power l_i^p with a common multiplier p = χ(u) ∈ Ẑ*. This is the ambient group from which ĜT-type groups are later cut out by S_3-symmetry; the previous page takes the commutant of S_3.

On p. 23 Grothendieck gives a 'symmetric' coordinatisation that does not single out l_0, unlike the later Ihara/Drinfeld normalisation x ↦ x^λ, y ↦ f^{-1} y^λ f. An element u is given by:
- its multiplier p (19);
- three conjugators g_i ∈ π̂ (20), with u(l_i) = int(g_i^{-1}) l_i^p (21).
These are subject to the product relation (22) and to the condition that the u(l_i) topologically generate π̂.

This page:
1. Ambiguity of the conjugators. For fixed u, each g_i is unique only up to multiplication by an arbitrary element l_i^{α_i} of L_i (α_i ∈ Ẑ), on the side that commutes with l_i^p. Composing u with an inner automorphism replaces (g_i) by (g g_i).
2. Composition law (23). If v has multiplier q and conjugators h_i, then vu(l_i) = int(v(g_i)^{-1}) v(l_i)^p = int(conjugator) l_i^{pq}. The conjugator of vu is the product of h_i and v(g_i), in an order fixed by the convention for int.
3. The extension SΣ̂^!. It is defined as the group of pairs (u, (g_i)) with u ∈ Σ̂^! and (g_i) an explicit system of conjugators as in (21). It is an extension of Σ̂^! by Ẑ^{0,1,∞}, the choices of the α_i. Equivalently (marginal NB), it is the closed subgroup of Ẑ* × π̂^{0,1,∞} cut out by (22) plus generation.
4. The cocycle (24). The coordinate functions γ_i(u,(g_i)) = g_i satisfy a twisted multiplicativity: γ_i(vu) is the product of γ_i(v) and v(γ_i(u)), in the order fixed by the int convention. So (γ_i) is a crossed homomorphism (1-cocycle) on SΣ̂^! with values in π̂^{0,1,∞}, with SΣ̂^! acting diagonally through u.
5. The kernel. The kernel of SΣ̂^! → Autext^!(π̂,(l_i)) is identified with π̂ × ∏ L_i ≅ π̂ × Ẑ^{0,1,∞}. The next page makes the map explicit: (g,(d_i)) ↦ (p = 1, g_i = g l_i^{d_i}).

Purpose: build a rigid group-theoretic model, with a cocycle description, in which the S_3-symmetry and the rotation ρ (next page: σ_i(ρ u ρ^{-1}) = σ_{i+1}(u)) act transparently. This is in view of defining and studying the 'Teichmüller-type' group (later ĜT) and the Galois action.
errors: The order of the factors in the cocycle identity (24) depends on the convention int(g)(x) = g x g^{-1} versus g^{-1} x g. The struck-out version ṽ(γ_i(ũ))·γ_i(ṽ) is the correct one under the convention int(g^{-1})x = g x g^{-1}. The replacement as transcribed, ṽ(γ_i(ũ)γ_i(ṽ)), would be wrong for either convention, so it is likely a transcription error or a slip.

Formula (23) as written, int(u(g_i) l_i^u) l_i^{pq}, is garbled: superscripts (u, ^, the multipliers) are confused with each other. The correct conjugator for vu is h_i·v(g_i) or v(g_i)·h_i, depending on convention.

The kernel statement implicitly uses two facts. First, p = 1 is forced for an inner automorphism; this holds because l_i maps to a basis element of the abelianisation Ẑ^2. Second, π̂ has trivial centre, so π̂ embeds. Both are true but are not stated on the page.

ideas.what: Description of an inertia-preserving automorphism of π̂_1(P^1 − 3 pts) by a multiplier in Ẑ* and three conjugators (g_0, g_1, g_∞) satisfying the product relation
ideas.modern_name: Parametrisation of ĜT / Galois elements by (λ, f); here in a symmetric three-conjugator form
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (1985-86, pro-ℓ case); Drinfeld (1990); Lochak–Schneps; Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Not in Esquisse d'un programme in this explicit form

ideas.what: Extension SΣ̂^! of the admissible automorphism group by Ẑ^{0,1,∞} of choices of conjugators modulo inertia
ideas.modern_name: Profinite analogue of the boundary-framed mapping class group / ribbon (framed) braid extension; tangential-basepoint rigidification
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura–Schneps and Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps (ribbon/framed versions of ĜT actions); Hoshi–Mochizuki (cuspidal inertia, tripods)

ideas.what: Coordinate functions γ_i forming a 1-cocycle with values in π̂^{0,1,∞}
ideas.modern_name: Crossed homomorphism / Ihara's f_σ cocycle on the Galois group

ideas.what: Kernel of SΣ̂^! → Autext^! identified with π̂ × Ẑ^3
ideas.modern_name: Inner automorphisms times boundary (Dehn-twist-like) inertia; analogue of mapping classes of the pair of pants fixing boundary

missed.claim: Grothendieck rigidifies the outer action by keeping explicit conjugators modulo the inertia groups L_i. This gives an extension by Ẑ^{0,1,∞}, a profinite analogue of twists around the three boundary components of the pair of pants. In this sense it is a 'framed/ribbon' version of the ĜT setting, formulated in 1981 in fully S_3-symmetric form. Later literature arrived at such framed variants separately (ribbon braids, tangential basepoints) and normalises asymmetrically (g_0 = 1).
missed.quote: Si on désigne par SΣ̂^! l'extension de Σ̂^! par Ẑ^{0,1,∞} définie par les triples d'un u ∈ Σ̂^! et d'un syst (21) des g_i
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical precedent for symmetric, tripod-style coordinates on ĜT-type groups (compare the tripod constructions of Hoshi–Mochizuki). Mathematically, however, it is largely known.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but essentially routine setting-up of coordinates for the Galois/ĜT-type action on π̂_1 of the tripod. The historical interest is that it is 1981 and uses a symmetric three-conjugator presentation with a cocycle and a Ẑ^3 framing extension. The content matches what Ihara, Drinfeld and successors developed later, so there is no new theorem.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 reads approximately 'est unique, et g_i défini [à] multiplication à gauche près par un él. quelconque de L_i, soit l_i^{α_i}'. The 'du' should be 'de L_i'.
Line 3 reads roughly 'Les groupes de u à intégrer ... gradués p, etc.' The insertion 'gradués p, etc.' is placed above a struck word ('couple'?); the reading is uncertain.

In (24) the replacement written above the struck formula appears to be ṽ(γ_i(ũ))γ_i(ṽ), with the struck version containing a hat on u; '$\tilde v(\gamma_i(\tilde u)\gamma_i(\tilde v))$' is probably a misreading of the parenthesisation.
Margin NB: '(g, g_0, g_1, g_∞) ∈ Ẑ* × π̂^{0,1,∞}'. The first coordinate is the multiplier p, so 'g' should likely read 'p' or a Greek letter.
Last lines: 'Le noyau [?] du groupe de SΣ̂^! → Autext^!(π̂,(l_i)) s'identifie au groupe produit (π̂ × ∏_{i∈{0,1,∞}} L_i) ≃ π̂ × Ẑ^{0,1,∞}'. 'groupe' at the start is likely 'noyau'.
In the paragraph about the structure, 'syst (21)' and the following words likely read 'qui explicite les conjugaisons des l_i' (uncertain).
